key_idea: Recasting the covering system problem as covering a finite grid with hyperplanes and bounding the uncovered set using a probabilistic sieve.
reason: While the translation of the problem into geometry and the use of a probabilistic sieve are highly innovative, the argument relies heavily on unilluminating numerical estimates and computer optimization to make the bounds work. This reliance on heavy computation obscures any purely conceptual reason for why the final result holds.
recognized: Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba (2022) On the Erdős-Selfridge problem
